## 5. PaymentStep integration

`PaymentStep` is **not imported, referenced, or rendered anywhere** in this file (confirmed via full read — no "Payment", "payment", "price", "cost", "$", "checkout", or "invoice" tokens appear in the 2003 lines except as described below). There is no payment/checkout step in the migration wizard flow at all — it goes straight from Review (Step 3) to `createMigration()` (line 579) and then to `MigrationProgress`. This confirms migration does not charge like domain-transfer within this component.

## 6. Pricing/plan logic

None. There is no destination-plan picker — Step 0 only lets the customer choose among their existing provisioned `servers` (server *instances*, not plans/tiers) via `ServerOption = { id, name }` (line 23). No price, discount, or cost figure is computed or displayed anywhere in the file. The only capacity/sizing UI is the storage-fit guardrail (`StoragePanel`, `storage` sizing logic lines 397–455) which is about disk bytes fitting, not billing. `sizing`/`SizingVerdict` (state line 248, rendered 756–771) is a workload-vs-plan-capacity warning ("You can upgrade this server from its Overview tab before migrating") — it links out to an Overview/Upgrade tab (line 767) rather than embedding any pricing UI.

- **Full duplicate render of StoragePanel and CompatibilityPanel**: identical components with identical props rendered once on Step 2 (lines 782–790) and again verbatim on Step 3 Review (lines 1060–1069) — same live-recomputed data, no new information, just repeated screen real estate.
- **Duplicated file/DB list recap**: Step 2 already shows checkable web roots/homes/apps/containers individually (793–950); Step 3 review re-lists them as a flat "📁 path" / "🗄 engine" text dump (1049–1058) plus a summary count row (1035–1046) — three different renderings of the same selection set across two steps.
- **Two "we migrate and start everything…" paragraphs** with near-identical wording appear at Step 2 intro (737–739) and Step 3 footer (1120–1124), plus a third near-duplicate description of the same mechanic inside the Docker section (896–903) and prereqs banner (744–750) — repeated explanatory copy instead of stating it once.
- **Forced separate "scanning" screen** (618–632) is a full page/state transition (not shown inline within step 1) purely for a network call that the copy itself says takes "under a minute" — no partial/live progress, just a spinner, blocking the wizard from showing anything else meanwhile; note it also mis-labels the Stepper as `step 1` (hardcoded) even though conceptually the scan corresponds to moving into step 2's data.
- **Advanced options collapsed by default in a `<details>` on the Review step** (1076–1118) — three consequential safety toggles (overwrite target data, rename clones, copy SSH keys) are hidden behind a click at the very last step, right before the "Start migration" commit action, rather than being surfaced earlier or more prominently.
- **"Advanced: add another folder" is also a hidden `<details>`** on Step 2 (984–1025) — for a scan-based tool, manually adding paths is a plausible common need (e.g., anything the scanner missed) but is de-emphasized behind a disclosure toggle rather than a visible affordance.
- **No forward navigation shortcuts**: Step 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 is strictly linear via Continue/Back buttons (1128–1163); nothing lets an expert user (e.g., re-running a migration to the same server with the same source) skip steps or reuse previous inputs — every field resets to defaults per session/mount.
- **`useVolumeForDocker` toggle is duplicated** inside `StoragePanel`, which itself is rendered twice (Step 2 and Step 3) — meaning the exact same toggle control with the exact same state exists in two places in the DOM tree simultaneously across the wizard's lifecycle (not simultaneously on screen, but functionally redundant markup/logic, lines 1278–1310 within a component instantiated twice, 782–787 and 1061–1067).
- **Databases section offers no control at all** (878–892) — unlike every other detected-item category (web roots, apps, homes, docker mounts) which get individual checkboxes, databases are all-or-nothing with just a "no password needed" explanation repeated near-identically in two places (Step 1 box, lines 722–728, and Step 2 box, 875–892).
- **MigrationRemediation and PostMigrationDns and MigrationRollback are three separate cards** stacked vertically post-completion (1480–1539) each re-explaining a "your old server is untouched"/"nothing is lost" type message in slightly different words (compare 1496–1497, 1577–1579, 1730–1734) — same underlying fact (read-only source access) restated three times in three different UI cards.
